topics.label: Retama
topics.description: Broom-form shrub with slender green shoots and yellow axillary flower clusters. The UAL account places it in retama scrub, sometimes pioneering ramblas, across varied substrates.
topics.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Slender, flexible grey-green shoots, losing their small leaves early; small yellow pea flowers in short lateral clusters. Yellow-flowered R. sphaerocarpa, rather than white-flowered R. monosperma.
plant_profile.growth_form: Airy shrub with arching, nearly leafless green shoots and small yellow flower clusters.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

topics.label: Esparto
topics.description: Robust tussock grass with long leaves that can roll into tubes. It forms dry grasslands known as espartales or atochares; this species identity is distinct from the habitat topic.
topics.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Also known as Stipa tenacissima. Dense basal tussock of long, tough rolled leaves. Shown without flowers; flowering plants have slender stems with narrow panicles and awned spikelets.
plant_profile.growth_form: Dense basal tussock of rolled leaves with retained straw-coloured leaf bases; shown without flowers.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

topics.label: Thyme
topics.description: Low aromatic woody thyme with narrow rolled-margin leaves and pink flowers. The cited account concerns subsp. hyemalis in southeastern Iberian scrub and thyme communities.
topics.name_note: Topic retains Thymus hyemalis; the principal detailed account is specifically subsp. hyemalis.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Small woody stems with tiny opposite, narrow rolled-margin leaves; compact terminal heads of pink, two-lipped flowers. The poster specifies winter thyme.
plant_profile.growth_form: Low woody subshrub forming a compact twiggy mound with small pink flower heads.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

topics.label: Rosemary
topics.description: Evergreen upright aromatic shrub with opposite narrow leaves, recurved margins and pale felted undersides. UAM records Rosmarinus officinalis and Salvia rosmarinus as synonyms.
topics.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Also called Rosmarinus officinalis. Opposite narrow leaves have rolled-under edges, dark green upper surfaces and whitish undersides. Small pale blue-lavender, two-lipped flowers sit near the stems; this is rosemary, not lavender.
plant_profile.growth_form: Upright branching evergreen shrub with narrow leaves; shown in an unpruned form.
plant_profile.basis: Illustration review notes; botanical references are attached to the image records.

topics.label: Joint pine

topics.name_note: Names reconciled with the old-app catalogue and the cited botanical identity. Common names vary.

plant_profile.identifying_features: Dense, slender green jointed stems with tiny scale-like leaves at the nodes and older grey woody branches. findings.label: Source-specific watercourse and jujube communities
findings.text: UAL describes warm Mediterranean watercourses with oleander and several Tamarix species. At Torre García, Ziziphus lotus dominates jujube scrub; Lycium intricatum is a companion and Thymus hyemalis occurs in openings. Its Tabernas discussion also names rosemary scrub. These are habitat descriptions, not mixed-planting trials.

findings.label: Retama ecology and symbiosis context
findings.text: The UAL Retama account describes photosynthetic green shoots, short-lived leaves, Rhizobium symbiosis and arbuscular mycorrhiza. It places the plant in retama scrub and sometimes as a rambla pioneer, from sea level to 1500 m. These species-specific observations do not imply that every legume fixes nitrogen or establish a treatment recommendation.

findings.label: Esparto leaves respond to water conditions
findings.text: The UAL account describes rolled leaves that reduce water loss and can unfold in wetter conditions, arbuscular mycorrhiza, and regrowth from underground parts after fire. It describes dry tussock grasslands from sea level to 1500 m in southeastern Iberia; this is not a planting-success prediction.

findings.label: Winter thyme avoids summer drought through seasonal timing
findings.text: The cited subsp. hyemalis account describes reproduction before summer drought, subsequent summer rest and rolled hairy leaf margins. It explicitly lacks species-specific mycorrhizal evidence, although other Thymus species have been studied. No inoculation recommendation is established.

findings.label: Ephedra cones and evidence limits
findings.text: Ephedra fragilis is dioecious; the female illustration shows fleshy cone structures, not ordinary fruit. The source describes green photosynthetic shoots and arid scrub membership, while noting that cited mycorrhizal evidence concerns other Ephedra species.

findings.label: Wild jujube provides shelter and supports soil formation
findings.text: The UAM factsheet describes the thorny deciduous shrub as shelter for animals and plants, with soil-formation and erosion-control functions. These are source descriptions, not quantified survival benefits for a proposed planting mixture.
